Eli B: Heads-up: scheduling a thermal/driver maintenance in az24 tonight 01:00-03:00 UTC to patch nvlink flaps and apply a kernel micro-backport.
Marta V: Cohort size? expected capacity impact?
Eli B: Cohorts are 2 racks at a time (6 nodes). We'll sequence across 6 cohorts. Peak capacity hit estimated 6-10%. Backfill from saturn-standby where available.
Sam C: Customer protection? reserved pools?
Eli B: Yes, enterprise reservations locked to warm nodes. Non-reserved batch jobs may be evicted during drain. We'll lower autoscaler threshold to favor reserved.
ops-bot: Preflight kicking off: checking kernel versions, active-job-count, egress baseline. Preflight report: https://confluence.redwood/az24-thermal-preflight.
Marta V: Important: last event showed a KV cache cold start spike. Plan to reseed prefixes before opening a cohort.
Eli B: Agreed. Run order: drain -> reboot -> kv-seed top100 -> 8m soak on one node -> perf checks -> open rest. Abort if p99 > baseline+150ms or error-rate >2%.
sre-rotation: I'm on-call and will monitor from 00:50 UTC. Escalate to Eli if canary aborts.
Sam C: Cost note: extra cloud GPUs for backfill estimated at ~$650. Tag to INFRA-MAINT.
ops-bot: Egress baseline az24/saturn: 100-180MB/s. Expect transient +15-25%. Alert threshold set 240MB/s.
Marta V: I'll watch KV hit-rate and redis misses, will post after each cohort.
Eli B: I'll run the commands and post cohort completion pings. React with :thumbsup: to ack.
Marta V: :thumbsup:
Sam C: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Preflight OK. Note: automation will pause if nvlink errors >0.2% and notify #eng-infra-alerts.
